poems.title: Lord Onyx Blepman
poems.text:
I cup his face in my hands,
His face rubs against mine,
Our world shattered in pieces,
But I know we'll one day be fine.

He's more than a cat,
He's my very best friend,
Fled all that we knew,
But soon it will end.

Horrors we've seen,
And so much derision,
But with him at my side,
Nothing clouds my vision.

Aching bones from sitting so long,
My wheelchair is my prison,
But my void meows at me,
And snuggles so close,
He seems content if not happy.

He isn't dumb,
He knows something's wrong,
We keep moving from place to place,
But he's been so strong.

I'm transgender,
So they hate me on principle,
But Onyx's love,
Has proven unconditional.

In the darkest of nights,
When hope seems so thin,
Onyx's purrs remind me,
Of the strength within.

We’ve faced the cold streets,
And the stares full of spite,
But together we stand,
In the face of the fight.

With wheels as my legs,
And Onyx as my guide,
We navigate shadows,
With courage and pride.

Though hate tried to break us,
And tear us apart,
We rise from the ashes,
With fire in our heart.

Each dawn brings new trials,
But also new dreams,
And with Onyx beside me,
Nothing’s as it seems.

For love is our armor,
And hope is our shield,
In a world full of battles,
We refuse to yield.

So here’s to the future,
To the life we’ll create,
Where love conquers all,
And there’s no room for hate.

With Onyx’s soft purrs,
And my spirit so strong,
We’ll find our own place,
Where we truly belong.

poems.title: My baby Onyx
poems.text:
The way you put your paws,
On my soul and heart,
The way you carried me forward,
From the very start.

You are my best friend,
Even now that you're gone,
The way you'd grumble and groan,
Like an old man wanting kids off his lawn.

You'd make me smile and laugh,
Brought joy to a weary life,
Most of my life has been pain,
So much has been nothing but strife.

You gave me a void to scream into,
When things got too much,
Wrapped your paws around me,
Gave me hope I could touch.

Your body may be gone,
I no longer feel your weight on my legs,
But I can still feel you here,
Though I do miss your constant begs.

The way you'd be so entitled,
To a portion of all my food,
You'd use me as a bed,
But think my shifting was rude.

But we adored each other,
Had a bond unshakable,
People called it symbiotic,
It was truly unbreakable.

We lived in many states,
Endured homelessness and fear,
But everything felt possible,
With my void boy near.

Everything still feels possible,
Even though touched with sadness,
So you must still be with me,
That thought brings me so much gladness.

So my void who was my light,
In my darkest days,
You continue to brighten my world,
In so many many ways.
